At lower values of the SFD extinction, we find that the sky surface density of galaxies increases with increasing extinction, precisely the opposite of the effect expected from Galactic dust. We also find that the average color of the SDSS photometric galaxy sample is slightly bluer at higher SFD extinctions in this regime, again the opposite of the effect expected from Galactic dust. Even though these anomalies occur only for sight-lines with low SFD extinction values, they affect approximately 68% of the high galactic latitude sky in which galaxies and their clustering properties are normally studied. Although it would be possible to explain these effects with a mysterious component of Galactic dust, which is anti-correlated with the 100<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m flux on which the SFD extinction map is based, this model is not physically plausible. Moreover, we find that the surface number density of SDSS photometric quasars does not show any similar effect, as would be expected if the explanation were an unknown Galactic dust component. Considering these results, we suggest that the far infrared (FIR) brightness of the sky in regions of true low dust extinction is significantly “contaminated” by the FIR emission from background galaxies. We show that such an explanation is both qualitatively and quantitatively consistent with the available data. Based on this interpretation we conclude that systematic errors in the SFD extinction map due to extragalactic FIR emission are quite small, on the order hundredths of a magnitude, but nevertheless statistically detectable. Unfortunately, however, these errors are also entangled in a complex way with a signal of great interest to many “precision cosmology” applications, namely the large-scale clustering of galaxies.

articleTitle: A Possible Estimate of the Doppler Factors for Blazars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have studied the beaming effect and multi-band properties of blazars using a sample of 31 blazars. In the sample, the observed variability timescale, the mass of the central super-massive black hole (SMBH), and the flux densities at 4 energy bands (radio, optical, X-ray, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray) of each object were compiled from the literature. The Doppler factor was estimated in two cases: (1) considering that the Doppler factor is the same throughout the entire energy band, and calculating by using the observed variability timescale; (2) the Doppler factor is a function of frequency, i.e., the Doppler factor is variable in a different energy band. Based on the Doppler factor estimated in both cases, we find that the intrinsic flux densities at different energy bands are significantly correlated with each other.

articleTitle: Binary Black Hole Accretion Flows in Merged Galactic Nuclei
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We consider accretion flows from circumbinary disks onto supermassive binary black holes on a subparsec scale of the galactic center based on a smoothed particles hydrodynamics (SPH) code. Simulation models are presented for four cases; that is, a circular binary and an eccentric one, each with equal and unequal masses. We find that the circumblack-hole disks are formed around each black hole regardless of the simulation parameters. There are two-step mechanisms that cause accretion flow. First, tidally induced elongation of the circumbinary disk triggers mass inflow toward two closest points on the circumbinary disk. Then, the gas is increasingly accumulated on these two points owing to the gravitational attraction of black holes. Second, when the gas can pass across the maximum loci of the effective binary potential, it starts to overflow via their two points, and freely infalls to each black hole. In circular binaries, the gas continues to be supplied from the circumbinary disk, (i.e., the gap between the circumbinary disk and the binary black hole is always closed). In eccentric cases, the mass supply undergoes periodic on/off transitions during one orbital period because of the variation of the periodic potential. The gap starts to close after the apoastron, and to open again after the next periastron passage. Due to the gap closing/opening cycles, the mass-capture rates are eventually strongly phase dependent. This could provide observable diagnosis for the presence of supermassive binary black holes in merged galactic nuclei.

articleTitle: Discovery of a Possible X-Ray Counterpart to HESS J1804—216
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Suzaku deep observations have discovered two highly significant nonthermal X-ray sources, Suzaku J1804-2142 (Src 1) and Suzaku J1804-2140 (Src 2), positionally coincident with the unidentified TeV <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray source, HESS J1804-216. The X-ray sources are not time variable and show no counterpart in other wavebands, except for the TeV source. Src 1 is unresolved at Suzaku spatial resolution, whereas Src 2 is extended or composed of multiple sources. The X-ray spectra are highly absorbed, hard, and featureless, and are well fitted by absorbed power-law models with best-fit photon indices and absorption columns of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-0.3_{-0.5}^{+0.5}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.2_{-0.2}^{+2.0} \times 10^{22} \,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$</tex> for Src 1, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.7_{-1.0}^{+1.4}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.1_{-0.6}^{+1.0} \times 10^{23} \,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$</tex> for Src 2. The measured X-ray absorption to the latter source is significantly larger than the total Galactic neutral hydrogen column in that direction. The unabsorbed 2–10 keV band luminosities are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.5 \times 10^{32} (d/5 \,\mathrm{kpc})^2 \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex> (Src 1) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.3 \times 10^{33} (d/5 \,\mathrm{kpc})^2 \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex> (Src 2), where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> is the source distance. Among the handful of TeV sources with known X-ray counterparts, HESS J1804-216 has the largest ratio of TeV <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray to hard X-ray fluxes. We discuss the nature of the emission and propose the Suzaku sources as plausible counterparts to the TeV source, although further observations are necessary to confirm this.

articleTitle: Nature of Infrared Sources in 11 $\mu $m Selected Sample from Early Data of the AKARI North Ecliptic Pole Deep Survey
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the properties of 11 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m selected sources detected in the early data of the North Ecliptic Pole Deep (NEP-Deep) Survey of AKARI. The data set covers 6 wavelength bands from 2.5 to 11 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m, with exposure times of 10–20 minutes. This field lies within the CFHT survey with four filter bands (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g^\prime, r^\prime, i^\prime, z^\prime$</tex>), enabling us to establish nearly continuous spectral energy distributions (SEDs) for wavelengths ranging from 0.4 to 11 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m. The main sample studied here consists of 72 sources whose 11 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m AB magnitudes are equal to or brighter than 18.5 (144 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>Jy), which is complete to more than 90%. The 11 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m band has an advantage of sampling star-forming galaxies with low-to-medium redshifts, since the prominent PAH feature shifts into this band. As expected, we find that the majority (71%) of 11 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m bright sources are star-forming galaxies at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.2 \lesssim z \lesssim 0.7$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\rm IR} \sim 10^{10}-10^{12}~L_{\odot}$</tex> based on detailed modelling of the SEDs. We also find four AGNs lying at various redshifts in the main sample. In addition, we discuss a few sources that have non-typical SEDs of the main sample, including a brown-dwarf candidate, a steep power-law source, a flat-spectrum object, and an early-type galaxy at moderate redshift.

articleTitle: Photometric Observation and Numerical Simulation of Early Superhumps in BC Ursae Majoris during the 2003 Superoutburst
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We carried out time-resolved photometric observations of an SU UMa-type dwarf nova, BC UMa, during its superoutburst in 2003 February. The period of early superhumps is 0.06258(13)d and the amplitude is 0.04 mag. After the early superhump phase, common superhumps with an amplitude of 0.3 mag and a period of 0.064466(16) d developed. The change rate of the superhump periods (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{P}_{\rm SH}/P_{\rm SH}$</tex>) (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\rm SH}$</tex>: superhump period) was positive throughout the superoutburst. The superhump period excess (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon \equiv P_{\rm SH}P_{\rm orb}^{-1}-1$</tex>) is 3% and we derived a mass ratio of 0.13. We have modeled early superhump light curves including irradiation effects of the accretion disk and secondary star. The observed early superhumps can be reproduced when two-armed spirals appear on the accretion disk. The long-term data taken from AAVSO, VSOLJ, and VSNET indicate that BC UMa shows normal outbursts and two types of superoutbursts (short-faint and long-bright). BC UMa is the first example to show such two types of superoutbursts. The supercycle of BC UMa is between 600 d and 1000d. This suggests that BC UMa is an intermediate type of dwarf novae between WZ Sge and SU UMa.

articleTitle: MOIRCS Deep Survey. II. Clustering Properties of $K$-Band Selected Galaxies in GOODS-North Region
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the first measurement of clustering properties of low-mass galaxies with a stellar mass down to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_*\sim 10^9 M_{\odot}$</tex> at 1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< z < $</tex>4 in 24.4 arcmin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{2}$</tex> of the GOODS-North region with a depth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_\mathrm{AB}\sim$</tex>25. Luminous galaxies in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-band have a larger correlation length than faint galaxies. For color-selected samples at 2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< z <$</tex>4, distant red galaxies with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J-K >$</tex>1.3 show a large bias of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b\sim$</tex>7.2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>1.3 on scales of up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta\sim$</tex>100<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\prime\prime}$</tex> or 3.1 comoving Mpc, while blue galaxies with 0.5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< J-K < $</tex>1.3 have a weak clustering signal on large scales, but a possible strong small-scale excess at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta < $</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\prime\prime}$</tex>. For massive galaxies with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_*>rsim 10^{10}M_{\odot}$</tex>, we estimate the correlation length and bias to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_0\sim$</tex>4.5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{-1}$</tex>Mpc and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b=$</tex>1.9–3.5, which are much larger than those of low-mass (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_*\sim$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^9-10^{10}M_{\odot}$</tex>) galaxies. The comparison of our measurements with analytic CDM models constrains the properties of hosting dark halos, and indicates that the low-mass galaxies would be progenitors of galaxies with a typical luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L\lesssim L_*$</tex> in the local Universe. The blue galaxies in low-mass samples are more strongly clustered in more massive halos with higher occupation numbers than low-mass red galaxies. This fact suggests an environment effect due to the halo mass on the star-formation activity at high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex>.

articleTitle: Suzaku Discovery of Iron Absorption Lines in Outburst Spectra of the X-Ray Transient 4U 1630—472
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the results of six Suzaku observations of the recurrent black hole transient 4U 1630-472 during its decline from outburst from February 8 to March 23 in 2006. All observations show the typical high/soft state spectral shape in the 2–50 keV band, roughly described by an optically thick-disk spectrum in the soft energy band plus a weak power-law tail that becomes dominant only above <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 20 \,\mathrm{keV}$</tex>. The disk temperature decreases from 1.4 keV to 1.2 keV as the flux decreases by a factor of 2, consistent with a constant radius, as expected for disk-dominated spectra. All of the observations reveal significant absorption lines from highly ionized (H-like and He-like) iron <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}\alpha$</tex>’s at 7.0 keV and 6.7 keV. The energies of these absorption lines suggest a blue shift with an outflow velocity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1000 \,\mathrm{km} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>. The H-like iron <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}\alpha$</tex> equivalent width remains approximately constant at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 30 \,\mathrm{eV}$</tex> over all of the observations, while that of the He-like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}\alpha$</tex> line increases from 7 eV to 20 eV. Thus, the ionization state of the material decreases, as expected from the decline in flux. By fitting the profile with Voigt functions (curve of growth) together with detailed photo-ionization calculations, the total absorbing column, and the ionization parameter were estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1.0 \hbox{--} 0.7) \times 10^{23} \,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(6 \hbox{--} 4) \times 10^4$</tex>, respectively, for a velocity dispersion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$500 \,\mathrm{km} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>. This in turn constrains the size of the plasma to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^{10} \,\mathrm{cm}$</tex>, assuming a source distance of 10 kpc.

articleTitle: A Complete Survey of the Central Molecular Zone in NH$_3$
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a map of the major part of the central molecular zone (CMZ) of simultaneous observations in the NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3 (J,K) =$</tex> (1,1) and (2,2) lines using the Kagoshima 6 m telescope. The mapped area is -1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rlap{.}{}^{\circ}$</tex>000 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq l \leq$</tex> 1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rlap{.}{}^{\circ}$</tex>625 and -0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rlap{.}{}^{\circ}$</tex>375 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq b \leq$</tex> 0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rlap{.}{}^{\circ}$</tex>250. The kinetic temperatures derived from the (2,2) to (1,1) intensity ratios are 20–80 K, or exceed 80 K. The gases corresponding to temperatures of 20–80 K and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq$</tex> 80 K contain 75% and 25% of the total NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex> flux, respectively. These temperatures indicate that the dense molecular gas in the CMZ is dominated by gas that is warmer than the majority of the dust present there. A comparison of our observations with a CO survey by Sawada et al. (2001, ApJS, 136, 189) shows that the NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex> emitting region is surrounded by a high-pressure region on the longitude–velocity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l - v$</tex>) plane. Although NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex> emission traces dense gas, it does not extend over a high-pressure region. Therefore, the high-pressure region is less dense and has to be hotter. This indicates that the molecular-cloud complex in the Galactic center region has a “core” of dense and warm clouds that are traced by the NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex> emission, and an “envelope” of less-dense and hotter gas clouds. Besides heating by ambipolar diffusion, the hot plasma gas emitting the X-ray emission may heat the hot “envelope”.

articleTitle: Multi-Wavelength Analysis of 18$\mu $m-Selected Galaxies in the AKARI/Infrared-Camera monitor field towards the North Ecliptic Pole
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present an initial analysis of AKARI 18<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m-selected galaxies using all 9 photometric bands at 2–24<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m available in the Infrared Camera (IRC), in order to demonstrate new capabilities of AKARI cosmological surveys with this unprecedented wavelength coverage at mid-infrared (MIR) bands. We detected 72 sources at 18<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m in an area of 50.2 arcmin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> in the AKARI/IRC monitor field towards the North Ecliptic Pole (NEP). From this sample, 25 galaxies with probable redshifts of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z >rsim$</tex> 0.5 were selected with a single colour cut (N2-N3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 0.1) for a detailed spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis with ground-based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BVRi'z'JK$</tex> data. Using an SED radiative transfer model of starbursts covering the wavelength range UV–submm, we derived photometric redshifts from the optical-MIR SEDs of 18<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m-selected galaxies. From the best-fit SED models, we showed that the IRC all-band photometry is capable of tracing a steep rise in the flux at the blue side of the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) 6.2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m emission feature. This indicates that the IRC all-band photometry is useful to constrain the redshift of infrared galaxies, specifically for dusty galaxies with a less prominent 4000Å break. Also, we found that the flux dip between the PAH 7.7 and 11.2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m emission feature is recognizable in the observed SEDs of galaxies at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \sim 1$</tex>. This pilot study suggests the possibility of detecting many interesting galaxy properties in the NEP-Deep and Wide surveys, such as a systematic difference in SEDs between high–and low-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> Ultra-Luminous InfraRed Galaxies, and a large variation of the PAH inter-band strength ratio in galaxies at high redshifts.

articleTitle: High-Resolution and High-S/N Spectrum Atlas of Vega
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a digital spectral atlas of Vega covering from violet to the near-IR region (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 3900–8800 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{\AA}$</tex>), which has such a high resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \sim 100000$</tex>) and high signal-to-noise ratio (typically <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 1000–2000 on the average) as to allow a detailed line-profile analysis. In addition, theoretically simulated spectra and lists of lines predicted to have appreciable strengths are also provided, which may be useful for identifying or searching lines on the atlas. Besides, the spectra of Regulus (a representative rapid rotator) obtained at the same night are appended as a reference of telluric lines.

articleTitle: Astrometry of H$_2$O Masers in Nearby Star-Forming Regions with VERA I. IRAS 16293-2422 in $\rho$ Oph East
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on results of multi-epoch VLBI observations of H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex>O masers associated with a low-mass young stellar object, IRAS 16293-2422 in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex> Oph East, and a fringe-phase and position reference source, ICRF J162546.8-252738, using the VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry (VERA) for high-precision astrometry. We obtained an annual parallax of a maser feature to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi=$</tex> 5.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+1.5}_{-0.5}$</tex> mas, corresponding to a distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D=178^{+18}_{-37}$</tex> pc. We also found 10 relative proper motions of maser features with respect to the maser feature mentioned above. The motion of the accompanying young stellar object (YSO) has already been found in thermal continuum emission previously observed with the Very Large Array. The intrinsic motions of masers have been estimated from the relative proper motions after the YSO’s motion is subtracted from, and a systemic secular motion of the position reference feature is added to the proper motions originally measured. The intrinsic maser kinematical structure may trace a bipolar outflow.

articleTitle: Distance to Orion KL Measured with VERA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the initial results of multiepoch VLBI observations of 22 GHz H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex>O masers in the Orion KL region with VERA (VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry). With the VERA dual-beam receiving system, we carried out phase-referencing VLBI astrometry, and successfully detected the annual parallax of Orion KL to be 2.29<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\pm\;$</tex>0.10 mas, corresponding to a distance of 437<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\pm\;$</tex>19 pc from the Sun. The distance to Orion KL was determined for the first time with the trigonometric parallax method in these observations. Although this value is consistent with that previously reported, 480<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\pm\;$</tex>80 pc, which was estimated from a statistical parallax method using the proper motions and radial velocities of the H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex>O maser features, our new results provide a much more accurate value with an uncertainty of only 4%. In addition to the annual parallax, we detected an absolute proper motion of the maser feature, suggesting an outflow motion powered by the radio source I along with the systematic motion of source I itself.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Spectra of 29 Carbon Stars: Simple Estimates of Effective Temperature
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Near-infrared spectra of 29 carbon stars in the 0.9–2.4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m range were obtained by using a cross-dispersed echelle spectrograph. The target stars, which were classified into C-H, C-R, C-J, and C-N types, were selected from an atlas of Barnbaum, Stone, and Keenan (1996, ApJS, 105, 419). Because the stars are non long-period variables, the phase differences of the light curves do not strongly affect the spectra. The effective temperatures (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{eff}}$</tex>) of the carbon stars were estimated with errors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm\;$</tex>200 K by fitting our spectra at wavelengths of 1.35, 1.74, and 2.29<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m, with simple model spectra, while considering the H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-}$</tex> opacity minimum to be around 1.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m. At these wavelengths, molecular absorption due to CO, CN, and C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> is not strong. The derived effective temperatures are distributed between 5100 K and 2600 K, and highly correlate with the temperature sequence in Barnbaum, Stone, and Keenan (ibid.), although the stars with temperature sequences beyond 4 have similar temperatures near <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 3000 K. We also compared our results with values derived by other methods in the literature: the aperture diameter method, the infrared flux method, and some model calculations.

articleTitle: Effects of Compton Scattering on the Gamma-Ray Spectra of Solar Flares
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Using the fully relativistic GEANT4 simulation toolkit, Monte Carlo simulation was applied to the transport of energetic electrons generated in solar flares, and resultant bremsstrahlung gamma-ray spectra were calculated. The solar atmosphere was approximated by 10 vertically stacked zones. The simulation took into account two important physical processes: that the bremsstrahlung photons emitted by precipitating relativistic electrons are strongly forward beamed toward the photosphere, and that the majority of these gamma-rays must be Compton backscattered by the solar atmosphere in order to reach the observer. Then, the Compton degradation was found to make the observable gamma-ray spectra much softer than predicted by simple analytic calculations. The gamma-ray signals were found to be enhanced by several conditions, including a broad pitch-angle distribution of the electrons, a near-limb flare longitude, and a significant tilt in the magnetic field lines if the flare longitude is rather small. These results successfully explain several important flare properties observed in the range of hard X-ray to gamma-ray, in particular including those obtained with Yohkoh. A comparison of the Yohkoh spectrum, from a GOES X3.7 class limb flare on 1998 November 22, with a simulation assuming a broad electron pitch-angle distribution suggests that gamma-rays from this particular solar flare were a mixture of direct bremsstrahlung photons and their Comptonization.

articleTitle: A Tale of Two Spicules: The Impact of Spicules on the Magnetic Chromosphere
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We use high-resolution observations of the Sun in Ca II H (3968 Å) from the Solar Optical Telescope on Hinode to show that there are at least two types of spicules that dominate the structure of the magnetic solar chromosphere. Both types are tied to the relentless magnetoconvective driving in the photosphere, but have very different dynamic properties. “Type-I” spicules are driven by shock waves that form when global oscillations and convective flows leak into the upper atmosphere along magnetic field lines on 3–7 minute timescales. “Type-II” spicules are much more dynamic: they form rapidly (in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>10s), are very thin (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\le 200$</tex> km wide), have lifetimes of 10–150s (at any one height), and seem to be rapidly heated to (at least) transition region temperatures, sending material through the chromosphere at speeds of order 50–150 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>. The properties of Type II spicules suggest a formation process that is a consequence of magnetic reconnection, typically in the vicinity of magnetic flux concentrations in plage and network. Both types of spicules are observed to carry Alfvén waves with significant amplitudes of order 20 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Suzaku Observation of Two Ultraluminous X-Ray Sources in NGC 1313
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Two ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) in the nearby Sb galaxy NGC 1313, named X-1 and X-2, were observed with Suzaku on 2005 September 15. During the observation for a net exposure of 28 ks (but over a gross time span of 90 ks), both objects varied in intensity by about 50%. The 0.4–10 keV X-ray luminosities of X-1 and X-2 were measured as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.5 \times 10^{40} \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.8 \times 10^{39} \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, respectively, with the former exhibiting the highest ever reported for this ULX. The spectrum of X-1 can be explained by the sum of a strong and variable power-law component with a high-energy cutoff, and a stable multicolor blackbody with an innermost disk temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.2 \,\mathrm{keV}$</tex>. These results suggest that X-1 was in a “very high” state, where disk emission is strongly Comptonized. The absorber within NGC 1313 toward X-1 is suggested to have a subsolar oxygen abundance. The spectrum of X-2 is best represented, in its fainter phase, by a multicolor blackbody model with an innermost disk temperature of 1.2–1.3 keV, and becomes flatter as the source becomes brighter. Hence, X-2 is interpreted to be in a slim-disk state. These results suggest that the two ULXs have black hole masses of some dozens to a few hundred of solar masses.

articleTitle: Radiative Column and Light Curve of X-Ray Binary Pulsars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We examine the published light curves (LCs) of 117 X-ray binary pulsars, while focusing on the dependence of their light curves on the observed energy bands. It is found that the energy dependence of the LCs appears only when the X-ray luminosity is larger than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\;$</tex>5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times {10^{36}}\;$</tex>ergs<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>. Assuming that the behavior of light curve is related to the radiative accretion column on the neutron-star surface, this energy threshold can be considered as observational proof of the accretion column formation proposed by Basko and Sunyaev. Once we can grasp the existence of a radiative column, we can also obtain several useful pieces of information about the neutron-star properties. As an instance, we performed a statistical analysis of the orientation angle of the magnetic axis, and we found that the inclination angle of the magnetic axis should be small in order to explain the observed statistics.

articleTitle: Precision Fe Kα and Fe Kβ Line Spectroscopy of the Seyfert 1.9 Galaxy NGC 2992 with Suzaku
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present detailed time-averaged X-ray spectroscopy in the 0.5–10 keV band of the Seyfert 1.9 galaxy NGC 2992 with the Suzaku X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS). There is an Fe K line emission complex that we model with broad and narrow lines and we show that the intensities of the two components are decoupled at a confidence level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ >3\sigma$</tex>. The broad line (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{EW} = 118^{+32}_{-61} \,\mathrm{eV}$</tex>) could originate in an accretion disk (inclined at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ >30^{\circ}$</tex>). The narrow Fe <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}\alpha$</tex> line (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{EW} =163^{+47}_{-26} \,\mathrm{eV}$</tex>) is unresolved by the XIS at 99% confidence and likely originates in distant matter. A significant (narrow) Fe <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}\beta$</tex> line is also detected and we describe a new robust method to constrain the ionization state of Fe in the distant line emitter (e.g. the putative obscuring torus). The method does not require any knowledge of possible gravitational and Doppler energy shifts and we deduce that the predominant ionization state of Fe in the distant matter is lower than Fe VIII (at 99% confidence), conservatively taking into account residual calibration uncertainties and theoretical and experimental uncertainties in the Fe K fluorescent line energies. We argue that the narrow Fe <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}\alpha$</tex> and Fe <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}\beta$</tex> lines likely originate in a Compton-thin structure.

articleTitle: Search for Oxygen Emission from Warm-Hot Intergalactic Medium around A2218 with Suzaku
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We searched for redshifted O emission lines from a possible warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM) surrounding the cluster of galaxies A2218 at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z=0.1756$</tex> using the X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) instrument on Suzaku. This cluster is thought to have an elongated structure along the line of sight based on previous studies. We studied systematic uncertainties in the spectrum of the Galactic emission and in the soft X-ray response of the detectors due to the contamination building up on the XIS filters. We detected no significant redshifted O lines, and set a tight constraint on the intensity with upper limits for the surface brightness of O VII and O VIII lines of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.1 \times 10^{-7}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.0 \times 10^{-7} \;\mathrm{photons} \;\mathrm{cm}^{-2} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1} \,\mathrm{arcmin}^{-2}$</tex>, respectively. These upper limits are significantly lower than the previously reported fluxes from the WHIM around other clusters of galaxies. We also discuss the prospect for detecting the WHIM lines with the Suzaku XIS in the future.

articleTitle: The Infrared Astronomical Mission AKARI
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: AKARI, the first Japanese satellite dedicated to infrared astronomy, was launched on 2006 February 21, and started observations in May of the same year. AKARI has a 68.5 cm cooled telescope, together with two focal-plane instruments, which survey the sky in six wavelength bands from mid–to far-infrared. The instruments also have a capability for imaging and spectroscopy in the wavelength range 2-180<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m in the pointed observation mode, occasionally inserted into a continuous survey operation. The in-orbit cryogen lifetime is expected to be one and a half years. The All-Sky Survey will cover more than 90% of the whole sky with a higher spatial resolution and a wider wavelength coverage than that of the previous IRAS all-sky survey. Point-source catalogues of the All-Sky Survey will be released to the astronomical community. Pointed observations will be used for deep surveys of selected sky areas and systematic observations of important astronomical targets. These will become an additional future heritage of this mission.

articleTitle: Swift and Suzaku Observations of the X-Ray Afterglow from the GRB 060105
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Results are presented of early X-ray afterglow observations of GRB 060105 by Swift and Suzaku. The bright, long gamma-ray burst GRB 060105 triggered the Swift Burst Alert Telescope at 06:49:28 on 2006 January 5 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0$</tex>). The Suzaku team commenced a pre-planned target of opportunity observation at 19 ks (5.3 hr) after the Swift trigger. The X-ray flux faded during observations from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.8 \times 10^{-9} \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1} \,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$</tex> (at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0 + 87 \,\mathrm{s}$</tex> with the Swift/XRT) to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.5 \times 10^{-13} \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1} \,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$</tex> [at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0 + 94 \hbox{}{--} 101 \,\mathrm{ks}$</tex> with the Suzaku X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS)] in the 2–10 keV energy band. Following prompt emission and successive very steep decay, a shallow decay was observed from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0 + 187 \,\mathrm{s}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0 + 1287 \,\mathrm{s}$</tex>. After an observation gap during <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0 + (1.5 \hbox{}{--} 3) \;\mathrm{ks}$</tex>, an extremely early steep decay was observed in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0 + (4 \hbox{}{--} 30) \;\mathrm{ks}$</tex>. The lightcurve flattened again at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0 + 30 \,\mathrm{ks}$</tex>, and another steep decay followed from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_0 + 50 \,\mathrm{ks}$</tex> to the end of observations. Both steep decays exhibited decay indices of 2.3–2.4. This very early break, if it is a jet break, is the earliest case among X-ray afterglow observations, suggesting a very narrow jet whose opening angle is well below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1^\circ$</tex>. The unique Suzaku/XIS data allow us to set very tight upper limits on line emission or absorption in this GRB. For the reported pseudo-redshift of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 4.0 \pm 1.3$</tex> the upper limit on the iron line equivalent width is 50 eV.

articleTitle: Japanese VLBI Network Observations of Radio-Loud Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We performed phase-reference very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations on five radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies (NLS1s) at 8.4 GHz with the Japanese VLBI Network. Each of the five targets (RXS J08066+7248, RXS J16290+4007, RXS J16333+4718, RXS J16446+2619, and B3 1702+457) in milli-Jansky levels were detected and unresolved in milli-arcsecond resolutions, i.e., with brightness temperatures higher than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^7$</tex> K. The nonthermal processes of active galactic nucleus activity, rather than starbursts, are predominantly responsible for the radio emissions from these NLS1s. Out of the nine known radio-loud NLS1s, including those chosen for this study, we found that the four most radio-loud objects exclusively have inverted spectra. This suggests a possibility that these NLS1s are radio-loud due to Doppler beaming, which can apparently enhance both the radio power and the spectral frequency.

articleTitle: Absolute Proper Motions of H2O Masers Away from the Galactic Plane Measured with VERA in the “Superbubble” Region NGC 281
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on absolute proper-motion measurements of an H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O maser source in the NGC 281 West molecular cloud, which is located <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 320 pc above the Galactic plane and is associated with an H I loop extending from the Galactic plane. We conducted multi-epoch phase-referencing observations of the maser source with VERA (VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry) over a monitoring period of 6 months, since 2006 May. We find that the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O maser features in NGC 281 West are systematically moving toward the southwest and further away from the Galactic plane with a vertical velocity of 20–30 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> at its estimated distance of 2.2–3.5 kpc. Our new results provide the most direct evidence that the gas in the NGC 281 region on the H I loop was blown out from the Galactic plane, most likely in a superbubble driven by multiple or sequential supernova explosions in the Galactic plane.

articleTitle: The Far-Infrared Surveyor (FIS) for AKARI
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Far-Infrared Surveyor (FIS) is one of two focal-plane instruments on the AKARI satellite. FIS has four photometric bands at 65, 90, 140, and 160 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \rm m$</tex>, and uses two kinds of array detectors. The FIS arrays and optics are designed to sweep the sky with high spatial resolution and redundancy. The actual scan width is more than eight arcminutes, and the pixel pitch matches the diffraction limit of the telescope. Derived point-spread functions (PSFs) from observations of asteroids are similar to those given by the optical model. Significant excesses, however, are clearly seen around tails of the PSFs, whose contributions are about 30% of the total power. All FIS functions are operating well in orbit, and the performance meets the laboratory characterizations, except for the two longer wavelength bands, which are not performing as well as characterized. Furthermore, the FIS has a spectroscopic capability using a Fourier transform spectrometer (FTS). Because the FTS takes advantage of the optics and detectors of the photometer, it can simultaneously make a spectral map. This paper summarizes the in-flight technical and operational performance of the FIS.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Imaging Polarimetry of the NGC 2071 Star-Forming Region with SIRPOL
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We conducted deep JHK<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{\rm s}$</tex> imaging polarimetry of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 8<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$' \times$</tex> 8<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$'$</tex> area of the NGC 2071 star-forming region. Our polarization data revealed various infrared reflection nebulae (IRNe) associated with the central IR young star cluster NGC 2071IR and identified their illuminating sources. There are at least 4 IRNe in NGC 2071IR, and several additional IRNe were identified around nearby young stars in the same field-of-view. Each illuminating source coincides with a known near-IR source, except for IRS 3, which is only a part of IRN 2 and is illuminated by the radio source 1c. Aperture polarimetry of each cluster source was used to detect unresolved circumstellar disk/outflow systems. Aperture polarimetry of the other point-like sources within the field was conducted in this region for the first time. The magnetic field structures (from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 1 pc down to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 0.1 pc) were derived using both aperture polarimetry of the point-like sources and imaging polarimetry of the shocked H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex> emission that is seen as the dominant knotty nebulae in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{\rm s}$</tex> band image; both are of dichroic origin and the derived field directions are consistent with each other. The magnetic field direction projected on the sky is also consistent with that inferred from the 850<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m thermal continuum emission polarimetry of the central 0.2 pc region, but is running roughly perpendicular (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 75<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex>) to the direction of the large-scale outflow. We argue that the field strength is too weak to align the outflow in the large-scale field direction via magnetic braking.

articleTitle: Lyman Break Galaxies at z$\sim$5: Rest-Frame UV Spectra. II
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present spectroscopy results of Lyman break galaxies (LBGs) at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>5 in the J0053+1234 field. Among five bright candidates with z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$'$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;<\;$</tex>25.0 mag, two objects are confirmed to be at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\sim\;$</tex>5. The equivalent widths (EWs) of Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission of the 2 LBGs are not so strong as to be detected as Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emitters, and one of them shows strong low-ionization interstellar (LIS) metal absorption lines. Two faint objects with z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$'$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq$</tex>25.0 mag are also confirmed to be at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\sim\;$</tex>5, and their spectra show strong Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission in contrast to bright ones. These results suggest a deficiency of strong Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission in bright LBGs at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\sim\;$</tex>5, as discussed in our previous paper. Combined with our previous spectra of LBGs at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\sim\;$</tex>5, obtained around the Hubble Deep Field-North (HDF-N), we made a composite spectrum of luminous (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{1400} \leq -$</tex>21.5 mag) LBGs at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\sim\;$</tex>5. The resultant spectrum shows weak Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission and strong LIS absorptions, which suggest that the bright LBGs at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\sim\;$</tex>5 have chemically evolved at least to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>0.1 solar metallicity. For a part of our sample in the HDF-N region, we obtained near-to-mid infrared data, which constrain the stellar masses of these objects. With the stellar mass and the metallicity estimated from the LIS absorptions, the metallicities of the LBGs at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\sim\;$</tex>5 tend to be lower than those of galaxies with the same stellar mass at z<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim 2$</tex>, although the uncertainty is very large.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Rossiter–McLaughlin Effect in the Transiting Exoplanetary System TrES-1
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report a measurement of the Rossiter–McLaughlin effect in the transiting extrasolar planetary system TrES-1, via simultaneous spectroscopic and photometric observations with the Subaru and MAGNUM telescopes. By modeling the radial velocity anomaly that was observed during a transit, we determine the sky-projected angle between the stellar spin axis and the planetary orbital axis to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda = 30^{\circ}\pm 21^{\circ}$</tex>. This is the third case for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> has been measured in a transiting exoplanetary system, and the first demonstration that such measurements are possible for relatively faint host stars (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V \sim$</tex> 12, as compared to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V \sim$</tex> 8 for the other systems). We also derive a time of mid-transit, constraints on the eccentricity of the TrES-1b orbit (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e =$</tex> 0.048<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.025), and upper limits on the mass of the Trojan companions (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim$</tex> 14 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\oplus}$</tex>) at the 3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> level.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared and Mid-Infrared Spectroscopy with the Infrared Camera (IRC) for AKARI
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Infrared Camera (IRC) is one of the two instruments on board the AKARI satellite, In addition to deep imaging from 1.8 to 26.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m for the pointed observation mode of the AKARI, it has a spectroscopic capability in its spectral range. By replacing the imaging filters by transmission-type dispersers on the filter wheels, it provides low-resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta \lambda \sim$</tex> 20–120) spectroscopy with slits, or in a wide imaging field-of-view (approximately 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;\times\;$</tex>10). The IRC spectroscopic mode is unique for space infrared missions in that it has the capability to perform sensitive wide-field spectroscopic surveys in the near-and mid-infrared wavelength ranges. This paper describes the specifications of the IRC spectrograph and its in-orbit performance.

articleTitle: A New 60-cm Radio Survey Telescope with the Sideband-Separating SIS Receiver for the 200 GHz Band
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have upgraded the 60-cm radio survey telescope located in Nobeyama, Japan. We developed a new waveguide-type sideband-separating SIS mixer for the telescope, which enables the simultaneous detection of distinct molecular emission lines in both the upper and lower sidebands. Over the RF frequency range of 205–240 GHz, the single-sideband receiver noise temperatures of the new mixer are 40–100 K for the 4.0–8.0 GHz IF frequency band. The image rejection ratios are greater than 10 dB over the same range. For dual IF signals obtained by the receiver, we have developed two sets of acousto-optical spectrometers and a telescope control system. Using the new telescope system, we successfully detected the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{12}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 2-1) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 2-1) emission lines simultaneously toward Orion KL in 2005 March. Using the waveguide-type sideband-separating SIS mixer for the 200 GHz band, we initiated the first simultaneous <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{12}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 2-1) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 2-1) survey of the galactic plane as well as large-scale mapping observations of nearby molecular clouds.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Imaging Polarimetry of the Star-Forming Region NGC 2024
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We conducted wide-field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$JHK_{\rm s}$</tex> imaging polarimetry toward NGC 2024, which is a massive star-forming region in the Orion B cloud. We found a prominent and extended polarized nebula over NGC 2024, and constrained the location of the illuminating source of the nebula through an analysis of polarization vectors. A massive star, IRS 2b with a spectral type of O8-B2, is located in the center of the symmetric vector pattern. Five small polarized nebulae associated with YSOs were discovered on our polarization images. These nebulae are responsible for the structures of circumstellar matter (i.e., disk/envelope systems) that produce strongly polarized light through dust scattering. For the point-like sources, we performed software aperture polarimetry in order to measure integrated polarizations, with which we detected candidate sources associated with circumstellar material. We found five young brown dwarfs with highly polarized integrated emission. These sources serve as direct evidence for the existence of a disk/envelope system around brown dwarfs. We investigated the fraction of highly polarized sources against the intrinsic luminosity of stars (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\propto$</tex> mass), and found that the source detection rate remains constant from low luminosity (brown dwarfs) to higher luminosity (solar-type) stars. This result indicates that the relative disk scale-hight is rather independent of the stellar mass. We investigated the magnetic field structure of NGC 2024 through measurements of dichroic polarization. The average position angle of projected magnetic fields across the region is found to be 110<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\circ}$</tex>. We found a good consistency in magnetic field structures obtained using near-infrared dichroic polarization and sub-mm/far-infrared dust emission polarization, indicating that the dichroic polarizations at near-infrared wavelengths trace magnetic field structures inside dense (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{V} \lesssim 50$</tex> mag) molecular clouds.

articleTitle: X-Ray Study of Discrete Sources in NGC 1808 with Chandra
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We analyzed discrete sources in a typical starburst galaxy, NGC 1808, with Chandra in order to study the relation between X-ray and star-forming activities. We detected thirty-eight X-ray sources with an X-ray luminosity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\rm X}$</tex>) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{37}$</tex> erg s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> in the central 5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\prime}\times$</tex>5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\prime}$</tex> (13.4 kpc <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 13.4 kpc) region. About 90% of the hard X-rays previously detected with ASCA came from these discrete sources. Among the detected sources, sixteen sources had an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\rm X}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{38}$</tex> erg s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>. The number of luminous sources is nearly equal to that of M 82, although their concentration into the central star-forming region is lower than that of M 82. There are several soft X-ray sources with a temperature of 0.6 keV in the central star-forming region. The X-ray properties of the soft sources are similar to those of a H II region, or a supernova remnant. The existence of both luminous sources and soft X-ray sources indicates the star-forming activity of NGC 1808. However, we detected only a few candidates of high-mass X-ray binaries that would be produced by enhanced star-forming activity. This may be due to the starburst age of NGC 1808.

articleTitle: Dissipation of Magnetic Flux in Primordial Star Formation: From Run-away Phase to Mass-Accretion Phase
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigate the dissipation of magnetic flux in primordial star-forming clouds throughout their collapse, including the run-away collapse phase as well as the accretion phase. We solve the energy equation and the non-equilibrium chemical reactions in the collapsing gas, in order to obtain the radial distribution of the ionized fraction during the collapse. As a result, we find that the ionized fraction is high enough for the magnetic field to couple with the gas throughout evolution of the cloud. This result suggests that the jet formation from protostars as well as the activation of magneto–rotational instability in the accretion disk are enabled in the presence of the cosmological seed magnetic flux proposed by Langer, Puget, and Aghanim (2003, Phys. Rev. D67, 43505).

articleTitle: Probing the Disk–Jet Connection of the Radio Galaxy 3C 120 Observed with Suzaku
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on deep (40ks <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 4) observations of the bright broad line radio galaxy 3C 120 using Suzaku. The observations were spaced one week apart, and sampled a range of continuum fluxes. An excellent broadband spectrum was obtained over two decades of frequency (0.6 to 50 keV) within each 40ks exposure. We clearly resolved the iron K emission-line complex, finding that it consists of a narrow K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> core (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma \simeq$</tex> 110 eV or an EW of 60 eV), a 6.9 keV line, and an underlying broad iron line. Our confirmation of the broad line contrasts with the XMM-Newton observation in 2003, where the broad line was not required. The most natural interpretation of the broad line is iron K line emission from a face-on accretion disk that is truncated at ~ 10 r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>. Above 10 keV, a relatively weak Compton hump was detected (reflection fraction of R <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\simeq$</tex> 0.6), superposed on the primary X-ray continuum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \simeq$</tex> 1.75. Thanks to the good photon statistics and low background of the Suzaku data, we clearly confirm the spectral evolution of 3C 120, whereby the variability amplitude decreases with increasing energy. More strikingly, we discovered that the variability is caused by a steep power-law component of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \simeq$</tex> 2.7, possibly related to non-thermal jet emission. We discuss our findings in the context of similarities and differences between radio-loud/quiet objects.

articleTitle: Stellar Contents of Two Intermediate Age Clusters: NGC 1912 and NGC 1907
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present CCD photometry in a wide field around two open clusters, NGC 1912 and NGC 1907. The stellar surface density profiles indicate that the radii of the clusters NGC 1912 and NGC 1907 are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim14^{\prime}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim6^{\prime}$</tex> respectively. The core of the cluster NGC 1907 is found to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\rlap{.}^{\prime}6\pm 0\rlap{.}^{\prime}3$</tex>, whereas the core of the cluster NGC 1912 could not be defined due to its significant variation with the limiting magnitude. The clusters are situated at distances of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1400\pm100$</tex> pc (NGC 1912) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1760\pm100$</tex> pc (NGC 1907), indicating that in spite of their close locations on the sky they may be formed in different parts of the Galaxy. Although the mass functions for the clusters are quite noisy, in the given mass range the slopes of the mass functions for clusters NGC 1912 and NGC 1907 turn out to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1.12\pm0.30$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1.23\pm0.21$</tex>, respectively, which are in agreement with the Salpeter value. Because the ages of the clusters are much higher than the estimated relaxation time-scales, dynamical relaxation may be one of the reasons for the observed mass segregation in the clusters. A comparison of the observed CMDs of the clusters with the synthetic CMDs gives a photometric binary content as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\pm10\%$</tex> (mass range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.0 \le M_\odot \le 3.1$</tex>) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\pm10\%$</tex> (mass range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.2\le M_\odot \le 3.2$</tex>) in the case of NGC 1912 and NGC 1907, respectively.

Author Keywords: open clusters and associations: individual (NGC 1912, NGC 1907)

articleTitle: Searching for a Companion Star of Tycho’s Type Ia Supernova with Optical Spectroscopic Observations
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on our first results of photometric and spectroscopic observations for Tycho’s supernova remnant (SNR Tycho) to search for the companion star of a type Ia supernova. From photometric observations using Suprime-Cam on the Subaru Telescope, we have picked up stars brighter than 22 mag (in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>-band) for spectroscopy, which are located within a circular region with a radius of 30<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\prime\prime}$</tex> around the center of SNR Tycho. If the ejecta of young supernova remnants, such as SNR Tycho, have a sufficient amount of Fe I, we should be able to detect absorption lines at 3720 Å and associated with transitions from the ground state of Fe I in the spectrum of the companion star. To identify the companion star of a SN Ia using these characteristic absorption lines of Fe I, we performed optical low-resolution spectroscopy of their targets using FOCAS on the Subaru Telescope. In our spectroscopic observations, we obtained spectra of 17 stars in the SNR Tycho region and compared them with template stellar spectra. We detect significant absorption lines from two stars at 3720 Å. In addition, spectra of four stars also have possible absorption lines. Since the widths of their absorption lines are broad, it is likely that the detected absorptions are due to Fe I in the expanding ejecta of SNR Tycho. However, none of stars exhibit a clear red wing in the observed profiles of the absorption, though a star in the background of the SNR should show it. Hence, we suggest another interpretation, that the detected absorption lines might be caused by the peculiarity of stars. Though Tycho(G) was raised as a candidate of the companion star of Tycho’s supernova in a previous study, we did not obtain evidence supporting the previous research. On the contrary, a star named Tycho(E) has an absorption line at 3720 Å, and its projected position is close to the center of SNR Tycho. Based on our observations, Tycho(E) is a new candidate as the companion star of Tycho’s supernova.

articleTitle: Dependence of Temporal Properties on Energy in Long-Lag, Wide-Pulse Gamma-Ray Bursts
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We employed a sample by Norris et al. (2005, ApJ, 625, 324) to study the dependence of the pulse temporal properties on energy in long-lag, wide-pulse gamma-ray bursts. Our analysis shows that the pulse peak time, rise time scale, and decay time scale are power-law functions of energy, which is a preliminary report on the relationships between the three quantities and energy. The power-law indexes associated with the pulse width, rise time scale, and decay time scale are correlated, and the correlation between the indexes associated with the pulse width and the decay time scale is more obvious. In addition, we have found that the pulse peak lag is strongly correlated with the CCF lag, but the centroid lag is less correlated with the peak lag and the CCF lag. Based on these results and some previous investigations, we tend to believe that all energy-dependent pulse temporal properties may come from the joint contribution of both the hydrodynamic processes of the outflows and the curvature effect, where the energy-dependent spectral lag may be mainly dominated by the dynamic process, and the energy-dependent pulse width may be mainly determined by the curvature effect.

articleTitle: Nobeyama CO Atlas of Nearby Spiral Galaxies: Distribution of Molecular Gas in Barred and Nonbarred Spiral Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The data from a CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> = 1–0) mapping survey of 40 nearby spiral galaxies, performed with the Nobeyama 45 m telescope, are presented. The criteria of the sample selection were: (1) RC3 morphological type ranging from Sa to Scd, (2) distance of less than 25 Mpc, (3) inclination angle less than 79<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex> (RC3), (4) flux at 100<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m higher than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 10 Jy, and (5) spiral structure not destroyed by any interaction. The maps of CO cover most of the optical disk of the galaxies. We investigated the influence of bars on the distribution of molecular gas in spiral galaxies using these data. We confirmed that the degree of the central concentration is higher in barred spirals than in nonbarred spirals, as shown by previous studies. Furthermore, we present observational evidence that bars are efficient in driving molecular gas that lies within the bar length toward the center, while the role in bringing gas in from the outer parts of the disks is small. The transported gas accounts for about half of the molecular gas within the central region in barred spiral galaxies. We found a correlation between the degree of central concentration and the bar strength. Galaxies with stronger bars tend to have a higher central concentration. The correlation implies that stronger bars accumulate molecular gas toward the center more efficiently. These results are consistent with long-lived bars.

articleTitle: AKARI Infrared Imaging of Reflection Nebulae IC4954 and IC4955
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the observations of the reflection nebulae IC4954 and IC4955 region with the Infrared Camera and the Far-Infrared Surveyor (FIS) on board the infrared astronomical satellite AKARI during its performance verification phase. We obtained 7 band images from 7 to 160<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m with higher spatial resolution and higher sensitivities than previous observations. The spatial variation in the mid-infrared color suggests that the star-formation in IC4954/4955 is progressing from south-west to north-east. The FIS 4-band data from 65<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m to 160<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>m allow us to correctly estimate the total infrared luminosity from the region, which is about one sixth of the energy emitted from the existing stellar sources.
